top.title: Kano varsity bans students, lecturers from exchanging gifts
top.description: Northwest University, Kano, has prohibited students and lecturers from giving or receiving gifts in connection with university services, warning that anyone who violates the directive will face disciplinary action. The university classified the practice as corruption and serious misconduct, stressing that the ban applies to both staff and students, irrespective of the intentions behind the gifts. The Registrar, Isyaku Adamu, announced the directive in a statement issued on Friday, following public attention generated by reports of students presenting gifts to lecturers recognised as the best level coordinators or lecturers in their respective categories. According to the registrar, the practice could damage the institution’s reputation and violate provisions of its Service Conditions and Regulations (2025), as amended. The university specifically identified the giving and receiving of gifts as acts of corruption and conduct capable of bringing the institution into disrepute. “Consequently, any staff or students found involved in giving and/or receiving gift items for university services rendered will be charged with committing an act(s) of serious misconduct and the university will immediately initiate disciplinary process against the staff or students according to the university’s regulations,” Adamu said. He added that offenders would be liable to sanctions under Section 16 of the regulations. The registrar consequently urged members of the university community to observe the institution’s rules, ethical standards and best practices to avoid disciplinary action. He also called on staff and students to take the directive seriously, adding, “A stitch in time saves nine!” Northwest University, Kano, is a state-owned institution established by the Kano State Government in 2012. It was renamed Yusuf Maitama Sule University in 2017 before reverting to its original name in 2024 following an amendment to the state law establishing it. top.title: Why Williams breached the 2025 F1 cost cap
top.description: Motorsport photo Williams' breach of Formula 1's cost cap regulations for the 2025 season was down to a difference in interpretation between its own finance team and the FIA adjudicators, relating to the company's restructure as the team moved assets into a new limited liability partnership. The Grove squad was found to have committed a "minor overspend breach" of £627,000 in the 2025 cost cap, although the FIA conceded that this was unintentional given its interpretation of the costs involved. Williams subsequently accepted the breach, which comes with a 1.5% penalty to its aerodynamic testing allowance, and an undisclosed fine. According to team principal James Vowles, Williams believed that a company restructure would count as a financial and legal activity, both of which are classed as exemptions under the 2025 cost cap regulations. The FIA did not agree. "We've gone back through it exactly now and what should we have done differently. And clearly, we should have done something differently as a result of it," Vowles stated. "And although the regulations aren't clear in black and white in its interpretation, the FIA is very clear on their perspective, which is the following: because you've moved contracts from one business to the next, that effectively for them is procurement, which is an included activity. "For us, we defined it as a financial and legal activity because it's literally taking a contract and changing a name on it. I can understand their interpretation, which is why we've accepted the breach. Alexander Albon, Williams Alexander Albon, Williams "But I hope that helps you understand why it's subtleties, not clarity, really, in that circumstance." As seen from its logs on Companies House, the scenario is that Williams - having traded as Williams Grand Prix Engineering Ltd since 1977 - had set up a new LLP: Williams Grand Prix Engineering Services LLP, and moved £27.8m worth of assets and liabilities into the new company. WGPE Ltd is the 99% partner in the LLP, with BCE GP LLC - a holding company understood to be managed by Dorilton Capital - registered as the 1% minority partner. By doing this, WGPE Ltd has a degree of legal separation in place and, for example, will usually not be liable for any debts accrued by the LLP. Vowles says that this is about ensuring a degree of future-proofing for the team, and another in a long line of expenses involved in bringing Williams up to date. As such, the majority of the £627,000 overspend has been tied up in incorporating the new LLP, and in transferring any legal documents and supply contracts to the new company. top.title: A closer look at Deportivo A Coruna’s Barcelona DNA ahead of La Liga clash
top.description: A closer look at Deportivo A Coruna’s Barcelona DNA ahead of La Liga clash Barcelona will look to maintain their winning run as they take on Deportivo A Coruna this weekend. The Catalans are leading the La Liga table by three points and cannot afford any mishap. However, they will be coming up against a Deportivo side that is more than capable of springing a surprise. Heading into this clash, Hidalgo has already heaped praise on Barcelona while talking about his Barça past, having started his journey at the Catalan club. Deportivo’s Barcelona DNA Hidalgo started his journey at Barcelona. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images) As reported by Mundo Deportivo , Deportivo A Coruna have deep connection to Barcelona, which runs far deeper than their head coach alone. Hidalgo was a member of the famed “Quinta del Troya” generation, joining the Barça academy as a youngster, where he struck up a close friendship with Xavi Hernandez. When Xavi later took charge of the first team, Hidalgo was even a candidate to lead Barça Atletic before he eventually joined Deportivo. After guiding Deportivo back to the top-flight at the first attempt, Hidalgo has built a reputation as a coach capable of reviving clubs under pressure. But he is far from the only member of his staff with Blaugrana roots. Oscar Hernandez’s remarkable eye for talent One of Hidalgo’s assistants is Oscar Hernandez, who spent more than a decade at La Masia and comes with a superb scouting pedigree. It was Hernandez who, alongside Isidre Gil, authored the very first report on Lamine Yamal, back when the Spaniard was turning out for La Torreta . The forward agreed to a trial and the rest, as they say, is history. Hernandez also played a key role in recruiting Take Kubo before continuing his own career abroad. He served as an assistant to Javier Mascherano with the Argentina national team and now oversees Deportivo’s day-to-day training sessions. A squad packed with ex-Barcelona stars Aubameyang is set to face Barcelona this weekend. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Apart from the coaches, Deportivo as a team is full of players with a Barcelona past. Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang is by far the biggest name, as is Marc Casado, who is on loan at the club until the end of the season. There are others such as Adama Traore, Arnau Comas, Adria Altimira and Luismi Cruz, all having passed through the club at various points. All of it sets the stage for an interesting clash this weekend, as Barcelona look to maintain their lead at the top of the table.

top.title: Jalen Brunson reveals why he prefers Stephen Curry over Magic Johnson as ‘GOAT’ NBA point guard
top.description: Credit: Joy Malone/Stephen Lam/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images In a discussion about the greatest point guard to ever play in the NBA, Jalen Brunson broke down why he chooses Stephen Curry over Magic Johnson. Having won Finals MVP while bringing an NBA title to the New York Knicks, Jalen Brunson has firmly put himself in the conversation as one of the all-time great point guards to play the game. However, that is a long list, and one that has some truly incredible names at the top. When talking about the GOAT NBA point guard, the conversation largely boils down to two names, Stephen Curry and Magic Johnson. Magic was instrumental in ‘saving the NBA’, and won five championships with the Los Angeles Lakers. Curry revolutionised the game with his shooting, and has four championships to his name. Brunson recently shared why Steph edges Johnson out on his list. Jalen Brunson says he personally prefers Stephen Curry’s shooting over Magic Johnson’s passing The Warriors superstar and the Lakers legend are completely different players. While Curry is a decent passer and has a dribbling package, his greatest strength has been his off-ball movement and three-point shooting. Magic was known for using his size and incredible court vision to unlock the offence, taking over the scoring only when necessary. When Brunson was talking about the GOAT PG debate with Dave Burd on the Roommates Show, he made his preference clear while breaking it down. “Totally different players. Me? I’m picking Steph Curry. I’m sorry,” Brunson said. “I got to have the person you have to guard when he steps on the court, no matter where he is on the court. That threat, where he just might be open, is scary for defenders. But then you have Magic Johnson who can make any pass or start any break. I prefer the shooting.” Brunson clearly explained his logic in picking Curry, and while many fans may disagree, the Knicks star seems certain of his opinion. Picking between Steph and Magic would be difficult for absolutely any basketball fan, but at least now fans know what the reigning Finals MVP thinks. One can even converse alongside play-by-play voice Kevin Burkhardt and seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady. But Andrews’ response revealed a lesser-known fear. “So, we have these things called IFBs in our ears,” Andrews said. “They’re like full molds. Mine are because I’m so worried about hearing loss. And then also, can get in my ears are my director, my producer, and some of the guys in the truck as well. So, I can talk to Casey, I can talk to GC about timing or about graphics or about any sort of stats.” During commercial breaks, Andrews confirmed that she could ask the technical team to turn her microphone up so she could talk to Burkhardt and Brady. top.title: Big blow for Real Madrid as Mikel Arteta confirms the return of Arsenal sensation
top.description: Big blow for Real Madrid as Mikel Arteta confirms the return of Arsenal sensation Real Madrid have been by far the best-performing team in the UEFA Champions League, having secured five wins in five matches so far this season. Jose Mourinho’s men firmly have one foot inside the top eight, and another win could further solidify their position as league leaders, with the coach quite happy with the current bunch . However, Real Madrid’s next game is against Premier League champions Arsenal, a daunting opposition known for their discipline and defensive solidity. Real Madrid are slated to face Arsenal on December 9, in what will be their final UCL game of the year. Arsenal handed huge boost Bukayo Saka picked up a knock against Bayern. (Photo by Leonhard Simon/Getty Images) With a couple of weeks remaining before they face Real Madrid, Arsenal have been handed a major boost. As reported by Mundo Deportivo , Arsenal coach Mikel Arteta has confirmed that Bukayo Saka has returned to training and will soon return to the pitch. Saka had picked up a hamstring injury on October 21 against Bayern Munich. He has since missed seven matches across all competitions. In Saka’s absence, Arsenal have won four matches, drawn two and have been eliminated in the Round of 16 of the League Cup against Fleetwood Town via penalties. Will Saka be fit to play against Real Madrid? Saka could cause problems for the Real Madrid defence. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) The report suggests Saka will not be fit enough to play in Arsenal’s next game against Manchester City in the Premier League. However, the English international may receive a few minutes against Brentford and Tottenham Hotspur before Arsenal host Real Madrid on December 9. There is a good chance Saka will be fit to play against Los Blancos . Coach Arteta has so far relied on the services of Noni Madueke, who has struggled to provide any real quality to the table. Saka, therefore, will be a major upgrade for Arsenal. He will cause a headache for a Real Madrid defence that has largely done well, especially on the left flank, with new signing Marc Cucurella offering ample solidity. The duel between Cucurella and Saka will be an interesting one to monitor and may well decide the fate of the clash, as the Gunners look to return to winning ways in the Champions League.

top.title: UEFA begins probe into Marseille, Besiktas fans clash
top.description: UEFA has opened disciplinary investigations into violent incidents involving supporters of Marseille and Besiktas during their respective Europa League fixtures on Thursday. The European football governing body announced the probes on Friday, following clashes between Marseille and Levski Sofia supporters in France and a confrontation between Besiktas fans and police in Georgia. In Marseille, several hundred home supporters confronted visiting Levski Sofia fans, leaving five Bulgarian supporters hospitalised. French magistrates have also launched an investigation into alleged intentional violence involving some Marseille supporters. Authorities are equally examining allegations of incitement to hatred following claims of Nazi salutes and provocations by Bulgarian fans. Meanwhile, Besiktas’ encounter with Israeli side Hapoel Beer-Sheva in Batumi, Georgia, was temporarily halted after clashes broke out between supporters and police. The incident followed the display of a pro-Palestinian banner bearing the inscription, “Revolt against the occupation, freedom for Palestine”, alongside Palestinian flags and chants against Israel. UEFA said the incidents contradicted its commitment to ensuring that football matches are played in an atmosphere of peace, mutual respect and sporting fairness. “The events witnessed at the above-mentioned matches run counter… to UEFA’s objective, enshrined in its Statutes, of ensuring that football matches are played in a spirit of peace, mutual respect and sporting fairness,” the governing body said. It added that it had appointed Ethics and Disciplinary Inspectors to investigate the incidents. The Besiktas fixture was moved from Istanbul to Georgia after Turkish authorities informed UEFA that the match could not be hosted in Turkey for safety and security reasons. The relocation came amid worsening diplomatic relations between Turkey and Israel following the outbreak of the Gaza war. Forest seized control through a stunning early volley from Igor Jesus, before Morgan Gibbs-White struck twice to steer the hosts to victory. top.title: “His Career Is Over”: Ryan Fitzpatrick Calls Out Aaron Rodgers For Seemingly Backtracking on Keyser Söze Plan
top.description: Aaron Rodgers. © Imagn Aaron Rodgers has found himself at the center of another NFL controversy over how he handled his situation with Mike McCarthy. Rodgers was released by the Pittsburgh Steelers after his explosive comments about McCarthy on The Pat McAfee Show. The quarterback accused his former coach of falling asleep during meetings and questioned his approach to managing the team. Former NFL quarterback Ryan Fitzpatrick addressed what comes next for Rodgers. Speaking on NFL on Prime Video, Fitzpatrick questioned why the quarterback felt the need to air his grievances in public. “I just think it’s fascinating because all we’ve heard from Aaron is the Keyser Söze thing. Once his career is over, we’re never going to see him again. He’s not going to live a public life. He’s not going to be on TV. He’s not going to do any appearances. And yet we’re one day into this, and he has to make sure that he has the final word and he writes the narrative. “…I would be shocked if he went to go play for another team this year, which means that his career is over,” Fitzpatrick said. Fitzpatrick’s comments came after Rodgers sent a text message to Al Michaels during the Steelers-Broncos Black Friday broadcast defending his decision to speak publicly about the McCarthy situation after being criticized by Tom Brady. “The code or sanctity exists to protect the integrity of the locker room, not to provide immunity from accountability for its leadership. They took this to the public. Never heard from the head coach. Then they leaked at 11 p.m. They also barred me from the facility. That’s why I went to McAfee,” Michaels quoted Rodgers as saying. The Keyser Söze reference was to comments Rodgers made in 2025, when he said he wanted to step away from the spotlight after retiring. “I don’t want the attention – I know that’s a narrative out there. When this is all done, it’s Keyser Söze. You won’t see me. I won’t be in the public. I don’t want to live a public life,” Rodgers said on The Pat McAfee Show, per NBC Sports . Will Aaron Rodgers Return for Another Year? Aaron Rodgers had previously indicated that the current season would be his final one in the NFL. top.title: Defining week for Republic of Ireland in World Cup bid
top.description: Republic of Ireland are aiming to reach a second successive World Cup [Getty Images] The Republic of Ireland are potentially just 180 minutes away from booking their spot at consecutive Women's World Cups. Standing in their way to next year's tournament are familiar foes in the form of Poland, who they beat twice in their qualifying group. They will play the Poles twice more, with the first leg in Gdansk on Tuesday, 1 December and the second leg at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin on Saturday, 5 December with the winner securing their place on the plane to Brazil. Ahead of a potentially defining week for Carla Ward and her players, BBC Sport NI looks at how they are gearing up for the massive play-off games. Republic of Ireland boss Ward signs new contract Mustaki out of World Cup play-off with knee injury Ward's new deal overshadowed by Mustaki's injury Mustaki ruptured her ACL while playing for Nottingham Forest against Liverpool [Getty Images] It's been a mix of good and bad news for Republic of Ireland in the build-up to the two games. There was the welcome announcement on Monday that head coach Ward had signed a new contract until the end of the Euro 2029 campaign. Ward's current deal was set to expire at the end of this World Cup qualification campaign and it will be a relief to the manager and players that she that will stay, irrespective of how the play-off pans out. It offers stability that the Irish have lacked in recent years and it is certainly well deserved given she has overseen 12 victories in her 19 games, including promotion to League A and excellent performances in their group against the Poles, France and Netherlands. Ward's legacy will really be enhanced if she can follow Vera Pauw in leading the team to another World Cup and she can fully focus on doing so now that her future has been resolved before this window. That announcement had followed the devastating blow that Ward had been dealt earlier on Monday, the confirmation that defender Chloe Mustaki would miss the play-off with a knee injury. Mustaki, who has been integral for the Irish as a left-sided centre-back under Ward, ruptured her anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) in action for Nottingham Forest against Liverpool in the League Cup last week. Ward said it was "a really difficult setback" for Mustaki, who also suffered an ACL injury in 2020 and was diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma aged 19. Her club announced that she would miss the rest of the season and she would also likely have to sit out the World Cup if the Irish do qualify. Ward did not call up a replacement to her 24-strong squad that gathered in Dublin on Tuesday and with everyone else fully fit, she will hope they have enough to get over the line even without Mustaki. nigeria.title: Kano varsity bans students, lecturers from exchanging gifts
nigeria.description: Northwest University, Kano, has prohibited students and lecturers from giving or receiving gifts in connection with university services, warning that anyone who violates the directive will face disciplinary action. The university classified the practice as corruption and serious misconduct, stressing that the ban applies to both staff and students, irrespective of the intentions behind the gifts. The Registrar, Isyaku Adamu, announced the directive in a statement issued on Friday, following public attention generated by reports of students presenting gifts to lecturers recognised as the best level coordinators or lecturers in their respective categories. According to the registrar, the practice could damage the institution’s reputation and violate provisions of its Service Conditions and Regulations (2025), as amended. The university specifically identified the giving and receiving of gifts as acts of corruption and conduct capable of bringing the institution into disrepute. “Consequently, any staff or students found involved in giving and/or receiving gift items for university services rendered will be charged with committing an act(s) of serious misconduct and the university will immediately initiate disciplinary process against the staff or students according to the university’s regulations,” Adamu said. He added that offenders would be liable to sanctions under Section 16 of the regulations. The registrar consequently urged members of the university community to observe the institution’s rules, ethical standards and best practices to avoid disciplinary action. He also called on staff and students to take the directive seriously, adding, “A stitch in time saves nine!” Northwest University, Kano, is a state-owned institution established by the Kano State Government in 2012. It was renamed Yusuf Maitama Sule University in 2017 before reverting to its original name in 2024 following an amendment to the state law establishing it. nigeria.title: UEFA begins probe into Marseille, Besiktas fans clash
nigeria.description: UEFA has opened disciplinary investigations into violent incidents involving supporters of Marseille and Besiktas during their respective Europa League fixtures on Thursday. The European football governing body announced the probes on Friday, following clashes between Marseille and Levski Sofia supporters in France and a confrontation between Besiktas fans and police in Georgia. In Marseille, several hundred home supporters confronted visiting Levski Sofia fans, leaving five Bulgarian supporters hospitalised. French magistrates have also launched an investigation into alleged intentional violence involving some Marseille supporters. Authorities are equally examining allegations of incitement to hatred following claims of Nazi salutes and provocations by Bulgarian fans. Meanwhile, Besiktas’ encounter with Israeli side Hapoel Beer-Sheva in Batumi, Georgia, was temporarily halted after clashes broke out between supporters and police. The incident followed the display of a pro-Palestinian banner bearing the inscription, “Revolt against the occupation, freedom for Palestine”, alongside Palestinian flags and chants against Israel. UEFA said the incidents contradicted its commitment to ensuring that football matches are played in an atmosphere of peace, mutual respect and sporting fairness. “The events witnessed at the above-mentioned matches run counter… to UEFA’s objective, enshrined in its Statutes, of ensuring that football matches are played in a spirit of peace, mutual respect and sporting fairness,” the governing body said. It added that it had appointed Ethics and Disciplinary Inspectors to investigate the incidents. The Besiktas fixture was moved from Istanbul to Georgia after Turkish authorities informed UEFA that the match could not be hosted in Turkey for safety and security reasons. The relocation came amid worsening diplomatic relations between Turkey and Israel following the outbreak of the Gaza war. nigeria.title: 2027: SDP candidate promises N200 petrol, free healthcare
nigeria.description: The presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), Dr Adewole Adebayo, has promised to reduce petrol prices to N200 per litre without subsidy and provide free healthcare if elected president in 2027. He also pledged free and compulsory education, increased food production, job creation and improved welfare for persons living with disabilities. Adebayo made the promises at an SDP town hall meeting with party leaders, candidates and supporters in Nasarawa State. He urged Nigerians to use the 2027 general election to determine the country’s leadership through the ballot, stressing the importance of electoral participation. Adebayo said the SDP had developed policy proposals to address poverty, unemployment, high living costs and other economic challenges facing the country. On fuel pricing, he said an SDP-led government would reduce petrol prices to N200 per litre without subsidy through improved efficiency and measures to address corruption in the petroleum sector. “We will give you petrol for N200 per litre without subsidy. We will sell it for N200, and NNPC will still make a profit because we will stop funding corruption,” he said. On agriculture, Adebayo said Nasarawa and neighbouring states had the potential to contribute significantly to national food production. “Nasarawa alone can feed Nigeria. Nasarawa, Plateau, Kogi, Kaduna and the Federal Capital Territory have the capacity to feed the whole of Africa,” he said. He also promised free and compulsory education, including measures to expand access to schooling for out-of-school children. According to him, an SDP administration would integrate children in the Almajiri system into formal education while ensuring they continued to receive religious instruction. On healthcare, Adebayo proposed establishing a Federal Medical Centre in every federal constituency and introducing compulsory medical check-ups four times annually. He also promised free medical consultations and medication, although he did not provide details of the proposed funding arrangements. On employment, the SDP candidate pledged to create more job opportunities, including for individuals living with disabilities. He also promised to develop Nasarawa’s mineral resources, including gold, coal, lithium and copper, to promote economic growth and improve the welfare of host communities. nigeria.title: Pete Edochie: Linc breaks down in tears as unusual calm rules Enugu residence
nigeria.description: By Benjamin Njoku & By Dennis Agbo Linc Edochie, the third son of the late Pete Edochie, could not hold back his tears when he saw his father’s corpse in the mortuary. The movie legend died in the early hours of Wednesday after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. He had taken ill and was rushed to a hospital in Enugu, where he passed away. Painting a gloomy picture of the atmosphere at the late actor’s riverside residence in Trans-Ekulu, Enugu-based actor and filmmaker, Steve Eboh, said Linc broke down the moment he sighted his father’s body. “When Linc stormed the mortuary and sighted his father’s corpse, he cried profusely and leaned on his brother’s shoulder. We consoled him and prayed for the family,” Eboh said. Eboh added that grief was written all over the faces of people whose lives Pete Edochie had touched during his acting career. “We thank God for a life well spent. He was a legend who touched so many lives. He was not just an actor, he was a global icon. Everybody knew him.” Our correspondent, who visited the late actor’s Trans-Ekulu residence, described a gloomy picture of desertion and sorrow. “Apart from a domestic aide seen at the premises, there was little indication of the tragic development that had thrown the family and the Nigerian entertainment industry into mourning,” he noted. A source familiar with the circumstances surrounding his death told our correspondent that the actor took ill on Tuesday night and was subsequently rushed to a hospital in Enugu, where he died at about 12:30am on Wednesday. According to the source, Edochie’s family had remained at the hospital since his death, apparently attending to necessary arrangements and coming to terms with the loss. The family’s absence from the residence accounted for the quiet atmosphere observed during the reporter’s visit. nigeria.title: Why I turned down Burna Boy’s 85/15 demand – Aristokrat boss, Peedi Picasso
nigeria.description: By Benjamin Njoku Peedi Picasso, CEO of Aristokrat Records, has opened up on why he refused to renew Burna Boy’s record deal, saying the singer demanded an 85-15 per cent revenue split in his favour. Picasso, whose real name is Piriye Isokrari said their previous deal gave Burna Boy 60 per cent, while the label took 40 per cent. He also revealed that the singer’s mother insisted he should only sign two-year contracts, a condition that influenced the label’s decision. According to Picasso, the proposed increase did not make financial sense at the time because the label was not making significant money from record sales. Picasso said live performances and endorsement deals were the major sources of revenue. He argued that accepting an 80-20 or 85-15 split would have left the label with a smaller share of the income despite the money it was investing in the singer. Picasso said the arrangement was difficult to justify for another two-year contract, particularly because the label was not entering a long-term deal. However, he admitted that his position has changed, saying he would now accept the terms he previously rejected. “Today I will take the 85/15 per cent now, but back then, it didn’t make any sense,” he said. nigeria.title: A Weekend For Proof
nigeria.description: INEC tests its systems on Saturday. Opposition leaders face their own test on Monday. Campaign violence makes both exercises more consequential. By Tuesday, Nigerians should have fresh evidence about two institutions seeking their confidence. INEC will have conducted its nationwide mock accreditation and result-upload exercise. Opposition parties will have had their scheduled opportunity to formalise cooperation in Abuja. The first must demonstrate operational readiness. The second must demonstrate an ability to act together. Both approach those tests amid a worsening concern: whether citizens can participate in the campaign safely. Wednesday’s attack on Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) supporters in Benin City, Edo State, confirmed by the police, followed Monday’s deadly violence in Delta. Edo police reported one person injured and ordered an investigation. The attackers’ political affiliations and any sponsors have not been established. That development changes the context of the coming days. Electoral preparation now requires visible progress on protection, accountability and public confidence alongside equipment and political agreements. Saturday: Let The Test Produce Evidence INEC’s mock exercise is scheduled for November 28, from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Nigerian time, in 17,676 selected polling units. It will test accreditation, election devices, and the uploading and viewing of simulated results. Registered voters in the selected units are expected to participate. The most useful outcome would be a public account of performance. How many locations opened on time? How many participants were successfully accredited? Where did devices fail? How long did uploads take? How were exceptions resolved? A rehearsal can reveal problems that announcements cannot. Finding a fault early allows INEC to correct it. Explaining that correction gives citizens a reason to have greater confidence. The exercise also has practical support from state governments. Lagos has cancelled Saturday’s sanitation exercise, while Anambra has postponed its own, to avoid obstructing participation. Those decisions remove an immediate obstacle. The remaining test concerns delivery at the selected polling units. Monday: What Will Opposition Unity Require? Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi, Seyi Makinde and other opposition leaders are expected at the November 30 summit. Their attendance and any signed commitments remain forthcoming. The APC says it is untroubled by the proposed gathering. The parties’ task is to define cooperation precisely. Joint election monitoring could be valuable. So could common procedures for documenting intimidation, sharing verified information and coordinating legal responses. Presidential cooperation presents more difficult choices. Supporters need to know whether their parties intend to campaign separately, endorse an existing candidate or pursue another lawful arrangement. A declaration of unity leaves those questions open unless it specifies obligations.

A small number of networks remain paused for maintenance, which Binance called standard practice and said was unrelated to the hack. The update closes out a month of phased reopenings. Binance confirmed the breach on Oct. 29, saying its initial investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that gave the attacker access to a service container, which was then used to submit unauthorized withdrawals. The world’s largest crypto exchange stopped all customer withdrawals for two days after the theft, Reuters reported . When they first reopened, customers pulled a net $4.7 billion off the platform, Binance said on Nov. 2. Binance covered the losses Binance said on Nov. 12 that it had completed coverage of the affected assets with more than $6.34 billion of company funds. The money came from a partial draw on its Secure Asset Fund for Users, part of its futures insurance fund and its corporate treasury, and the exchange pledged to rebuild SAFU to about $1 billion. Coverage is not the same as recovery. Binance replaced the stolen tokens from its own books, while about $2.85 billion of the stolen funds have been frozen remotely by the companies that issue them. The rest remains in the hands of the attackers. U.S. authorities have blamed North Korean hackers for the theft, which North Korea denies. On Nov. 23, the Justice Department moved to forfeit more than $1.1 billion in USDC that Circle froze, and said the U.S. has helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion since the attack. Launderers turn to THORChain and coinjoin The unfrozen funds are on the move. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test Russian bank VTB began letting brokerage clients buy and sell bitcoin in its investing app on Friday, a day after the Bank of Russia approved the knowledge test every Russian crypto buyer now has to pass. Starting Nov. 27, clients of VTB’s brokerage can trade cryptocurrencies in the VTB My Investments app, the broker said . For now, the trades happen over the counter rather than on an exchange, and access is limited to qualified investors, the legal term for Russians who meet wealth or experience thresholds, who also pass the new test. “In our model, access to cryptocurrencies will require qualified investor status and passing special testing,” Andrei Yatskov, head of brokerage services at VTB, said . He said the test would appear in the app on Nov. 27 and work like the bank’s existing tests for other instruments. VTB handles the buying, storage and record-keeping itself on Russian infrastructure. To trade, clients need to open a separate digital account at VTB’s digital depository, where the crypto is held, on top of their regular brokerage account. The bank received its digital depository and crypto exchange licenses on Oct. 6. “At the start, we will focus on buying and selling cryptocurrencies, and then we will introduce additional services as regulation develops,” Yatskov said. Eight questions before the first trade The launch came quickly after the regulator moved. On Nov. 26, the Bank of Russia approved the first basic standards for brokers and crypto exchange offices, setting the rules for the test. Every investor has to take it, qualified or not, and it is free. Buyers must answer at least seven of eight questions correctly. The standard lays out eight topic blocks, from regulation, technical basics and information security to stablecoins, low-liquidity coins, address labeling and blocked transactions, and volatility, with one question drawn at random from each. Investors who fail can try once more the same day, with different questions. Brokers are barred from sharing the correct answers with clients or telling them which questions they missed. A passing result stays valid for one year from the test date or the latest trade, whichever comes later. The test was the missing piece for Russian banks. When retail buying became legal on Nov. 17 , T-Bank said it was waiting on a market standard for testing, and VTB said it was waiting on the remaining rules. Under the broker standard, the industry’s self-regulatory organization has three working days after publication to send brokers the answer options and correct answers. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Founders A New York judge has ordered the founders of NovaTech, a cryptocurrency investment scheme that targeted Haitian communities, to pay more than $1.37 billion, closing out the state’s case against a couple who fled the country rather than answer it. Justice Anar Rathod Patel of the New York County Supreme Court signed the order on Nov. 24. It holds Cynthia and Eddy Petion and their companies NovaTech Ltd, NovaTech Advisors and NovaPay jointly liable for $1,367,023,585 in disgorgement and interest. New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the win on Wednesday. “Today’s historic judgment finally delivers some semblance of justice for the thousands of New Yorkers who were targeted by this merciless scam,” James said. “NovaTech cruelly targeted immigrant families through faith and community groups with the promise of a better life while robbing them of their life savings.” Where the $1.37 billion figure comes from The award matches what the attorney general’s office asked for in October . The figure starts with the cryptocurrency investors sent to NovaTech’s wallet at payment processor CoinPayments, which totaled about $1.16 billion from August 2019 through May 2023, according to an affirmation filed by the state. Prosecutors subtracted the roughly $26 million NovaTech actually moved to its trading platform, leaving $1.13 billion in principal. Nine percent annual interest from June 2023 through September 2025 added another $232.5 million. NovaTech’s traders lost about $18.2 million of the money they did trade, the filing said. Everything else paid out of the wallet, including so-called returns and recruitment bonuses, came from other investors’ deposits. Cynthia Petion was the only authorized user on the CoinPayments account, and the state says she approved at least $134.5 million in crypto withdrawals to wallets belonging to her and her husband. The judge also ordered the Petions’ earlier venture, AWS Mining, to pay about $1.46 million. Cynthia Petion owes a separate $4.69 million tied to her promotion of that scheme. Someone in the family knew someone in the village. An uncle walked the boundaries. The community remembered who owned what, and if anything went wrong, you had a face to go back to. However, my generation buys land on Instagram. I do not say that to mock anyone. I sell land for a living. When I started in real estate sales in 2023, two years after finishing a Mathematics degree at the University of Ibadan, I assumed buyers would care most about price and location. They do care. But what I hear most often is fear, dressed up as questions. Can I trust you? Is this land real? What happens if I miss a payment? After I pay, will someone come and ask me for more money? A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. She was asking whether the price I quoted was the real price. She had good reason to ask. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Yet the same law still allows a land-owning family, with the family head’s authority, to collect a customary fee for possession, the payment many people know as a “foundation levy”. So the honest answer to her question is not a simple yes or no. It depends on the land, the family, and what has been written down. Most first-time buyers have never been told any of this. That is the gap I keep coming back to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We learned how to save. Some of us learned how to invest in stocks, crypto or a side business. The people who used to stand in for the manual–the uncle, the community, the family lawyer everyone trusted–are often not part of how we buy anymore. So we improvise. Then you probably remember that voice. Deep, commanding and unmistakable, it often came with his signature red cap, traditional Igbo attire and a generous helping of proverbs. The actor was just as memorable away from the screen, where his sharp wit, outspoken nature and candid opinions made him a fascinating personality in interviews. He was never one to shy away from saying exactly what he thought, and that straightforwardness became another part of what audiences remembered about him. For generations of Nollywood viewers, Pete Edochie was the actor they could recognise before he had even finished his first sentence. He became one of Nigerian cinema’s most familiar faces, often playing kings, chiefs, fathers and respected elders. His breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart , a performance that helped establish him as one of Nollywood’s most respected actors. The veteran actor passed away in Enugu yesterday, on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, at the age of 79, following a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. Born in Zaria and originally from Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Edochie began his career in broadcasting in 1967, eventually rising to become Deputy Managing Director of the Anambra Broadcasting Service. He went on to feature in hundreds of films, including Igodo , The Egg of Life and Lionheart . Pete Edochie and Genevieve Nnaji behind the scenes on the set of the 2018 film Lionheart, where they played father and daughter Chief Ernest Obiagu and Adaeze Obiagu. Survived by his wife, Josephine, and their six children, including actors Linc and Yul Edochie , he leaves behind a remarkable body of work. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). The Grove squad was found to have committed a "minor overspend breach" of £627,000 in the 2025 cost cap, although the FIA conceded that this was unintentional given its interpretation of the costs involved. Williams subsequently accepted the breach, which comes with a 1.5% penalty to its aerodynamic testing allowance, and an undisclosed fine. According to team principal James Vowles, Williams believed that a company restructure would count as a financial and legal activity, both of which are classed as exemptions under the 2025 cost cap regulations. The FIA did not agree. "We've gone back through it exactly now and what should we have done differently. And clearly, we should have done something differently as a result of it," Vowles stated. "And although the regulations aren't clear in black and white in its interpretation, the FIA is very clear on their perspective, which is the following: because you've moved contracts from one business to the next, that effectively for them is procurement, which is an included activity. "For us, we defined it as a financial and legal activity because it's literally taking a contract and changing a name on it. sports.description: A closer look at Deportivo A Coruna’s Barcelona DNA ahead of La Liga clash Barcelona will look to maintain their winning run as they take on Deportivo A Coruna this weekend. Deportivo’s Barcelona DNA Hidalgo started his journey at Barcelona. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images) As reported by Mundo Deportivo , Deportivo A Coruna have deep connection to Barcelona, which runs far deeper than their head coach alone. Hidalgo was a member of the famed “Quinta del Troya” generation, joining the Barça academy as a youngster, where he struck up a close friendship with Xavi Hernandez. When Xavi later took charge of the first team, Hidalgo was even a candidate to lead Barça Atletic before he eventually joined Deportivo. After guiding Deportivo back to the top-flight at the first attempt, Hidalgo has built a reputation as a coach capable of reviving clubs under pressure. But he is far from the only member of his staff with Blaugrana roots. Oscar Hernandez’s remarkable eye for talent One of Hidalgo’s assistants is Oscar Hernandez, who spent more than a decade at La Masia and comes with a superb scouting pedigree. It was Hernandez who, alongside Isidre Gil, authored the very first report on Lamine Yamal, back when the Spaniard was turning out for La Torreta . The forward agreed to a trial and the rest, as they say, is history. Hernandez also played a key role in recruiting Take Kubo before continuing his own career abroad. He served as an assistant to Javier Mascherano with the Argentina national team and now oversees Deportivo’s day-to-day training sessions. A squad packed with ex-Barcelona stars Aubameyang is set to face Barcelona this weekend. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Apart from the coaches, Deportivo as a team is full of players with a Barcelona past. Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang is by far the biggest name, as is Marc Casado, who is on loan at the club until the end of the season. There are others such as Adama Traore, Arnau Comas, Adria Altimira and Luismi Cruz, all having passed through the club at various points. All of it sets the stage for an interesting clash this weekend, as Barcelona look to maintain their lead at the top of the table.

sports.title: Jalen Brunson reveals why he prefers Stephen Curry over Magic Johnson as ‘GOAT’ NBA point guard
sports.description: Credit: Joy Malone/Stephen Lam/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images In a discussion about the greatest point guard to ever play in the NBA, Jalen Brunson broke down why he chooses Stephen Curry over Magic Johnson. Having won Finals MVP while bringing an NBA title to the New York Knicks, Jalen Brunson has firmly put himself in the conversation as one of the all-time great point guards to play the game. However, that is a long list, and one that has some truly incredible names at the top. When talking about the GOAT NBA point guard, the conversation largely boils down to two names, Stephen Curry and Magic Johnson. Magic was instrumental in ‘saving the NBA’, and won five championships with the Los Angeles Lakers. Curry revolutionised the game with his shooting, and has four championships to his name. Brunson recently shared why Steph edges Johnson out on his list. Jalen Brunson says he personally prefers Stephen Curry’s shooting over Magic Johnson’s passing The Warriors superstar and the Lakers legend are completely different players. While Curry is a decent passer and has a dribbling package, his greatest strength has been his off-ball movement and three-point shooting. Magic was known for using his size and incredible court vision to unlock the offence, taking over the scoring only when necessary. When Brunson was talking about the GOAT PG debate with Dave Burd on the Roommates Show, he made his preference clear while breaking it down. “Totally different players. Me? I’m picking Steph Curry. I’m sorry,” Brunson said. “I got to have the person you have to guard when he steps on the court, no matter where he is on the court. That threat, where he just might be open, is scary for defenders. But then you have Magic Johnson who can make any pass or start any break. I prefer the shooting.” Brunson clearly explained his logic in picking Curry, and while many fans may disagree, the Knicks star seems certain of his opinion. Picking between Steph and Magic would be difficult for absolutely any basketball fan, but at least now fans know what the reigning Finals MVP thinks. During the recent episode of Calm Down With Erin And Charissa , Charissa Thompson asked Erin Andrews to talk about the interruptible foldback (IFB) that the broadcasters use while covering the games live to minimize the crowd’s noise. But Andrews’ response revealed a lesser-known fear. “So, we have these things called IFBs in our ears,” Andrews said. “They’re like full molds. Mine are because I’m so worried about hearing loss. And for my first hit, in our ears, in our IFBs, we get program. That’s what I get, so I can hear Kevin [Burkhardt] and Tom [Brady]. And then also, can get in my ears are my director, my producer, and some of the guys in the truck as well. So, I can talk to Casey, I can talk to GC about timing or about graphics or about any sort of stats.” During commercial breaks, Andrews confirmed that she could ask the technical team to turn her microphone up so she could talk to Burkhardt and Brady. The conversation could vary, but the threat is real. The health risks facing sideline reporters are rarely discussed. Subscribe to stay informed on the behind-the-scenes challenges shaping NFL coverage. “And then usually for the game, I take one ear out so I can hear what’s happening with the players, the coaches, the fans,” Andrews continued. “If it’s super duper loud, I put both my ears in. You can get a real massive headache.” To protect her ears from both external stadium volume and high-volume broadcast feeds, Andrews opted for custom-fitted, full-mold IFB earpieces rather than standard single-ear acoustic tubes. Even then, she faces a constant tug-of-war throughout all four quarters. Of course, it isn’t just Erin Andrews who has trouble with the loud crowd. sports.title: Big blow for Real Madrid as Mikel Arteta confirms the return of Arsenal sensation
sports.description: Big blow for Real Madrid as Mikel Arteta confirms the return of Arsenal sensation Real Madrid have been by far the best-performing team in the UEFA Champions League, having secured five wins in five matches so far this season. Jose Mourinho’s men firmly have one foot inside the top eight, and another win could further solidify their position as league leaders, with the coach quite happy with the current bunch . However, Real Madrid’s next game is against Premier League champions Arsenal, a daunting opposition known for their discipline and defensive solidity. Real Madrid are slated to face Arsenal on December 9, in what will be their final UCL game of the year. Arsenal handed huge boost Bukayo Saka picked up a knock against Bayern. As reported by Mundo Deportivo , Arsenal coach Mikel Arteta has confirmed that Bukayo Saka has returned to training and will soon return to the pitch. Saka had picked up a hamstring injury on October 21 against Bayern Munich. He has since missed seven matches across all competitions. sports.title: “His Career Is Over”: Ryan Fitzpatrick Calls Out Aaron Rodgers For Seemingly Backtracking on Keyser Söze Plan
sports.description: Aaron Rodgers. © Imagn Aaron Rodgers has found himself at the center of another NFL controversy over how he handled his situation with Mike McCarthy. Rodgers was released by the Pittsburgh Steelers after his explosive comments about McCarthy on The Pat McAfee Show. The quarterback accused his former coach of falling asleep during meetings and questioned his approach to managing the team. Former NFL quarterback Ryan Fitzpatrick addressed what comes next for Rodgers. Speaking on NFL on Prime Video, Fitzpatrick questioned why the quarterback felt the need to air his grievances in public. “I just think it’s fascinating because all we’ve heard from Aaron is the Keyser Söze thing. Once his career is over, we’re never going to see him again. He’s not going to live a public life. He’s not going to be on TV. He’s not going to do any appearances. And yet we’re one day into this, and he has to make sure that he has the final word and he writes the narrative. “…I would be shocked if he went to go play for another team this year, which means that his career is over,” Fitzpatrick said. Fitzpatrick’s comments came after Rodgers sent a text message to Al Michaels during the Steelers-Broncos Black Friday broadcast defending his decision to speak publicly about the McCarthy situation after being criticized by Tom Brady. “The code or sanctity exists to protect the integrity of the locker room, not to provide immunity from accountability for its leadership. They took this to the public. Never heard from the head coach. Then they leaked at 11 p.m. They also barred me from the facility. That’s why I went to McAfee,” Michaels quoted Rodgers as saying. The Keyser Söze reference was to comments Rodgers made in 2025, when he said he wanted to step away from the spotlight after retiring. “I don’t want the attention – I know that’s a narrative out there. When this is all done, it’s Keyser Söze. You won’t see me. I won’t be in the public. I don’t want to live a public life,” Rodgers said on The Pat McAfee Show, per NBC Sports . Will Aaron Rodgers Return for Another Year? Aaron Rodgers had previously indicated that the current season would be his final one in the NFL. In July, a reporter asked Rodgers if this would be his last season. “Yeah, this is it. … I thought last year might be it, but then Mike McCarthy got hired and I talked to my wife and she said, ‘You can do one more year,'” he said, per Brendan Howe. “No, zero debate,” he added when asked if this was his final decision. For now, Rodgers’ NFL future remains uncertain. He cleared waivers on Thursday and is now a free agent. sports.title: 3 biggest takeaways for Sixers following Cup road win over Pacers
sports.description: INDIANAPOLIS -- The Philadelphia 76ers were able to clinch the Eastern Conference's Group B in the NBA Cup on Friday with a 111-87 win over the Indiana Pacers . The Sixers held the Pacers to 34.9% shooting and just 5-for-37 from deep as Philadelphia led wire-to-wire on its way to clinching the group and advancing to the knockout rounds to face the Atlanta Hawks. LeBron James led Philadelphia with 21 points, seven rebounds, and six assists, Anfernee Simons had 19 points, Tyrese Maxey added 14 points and six assists, and VJ Edgecombe had nine points, five rebounds, and seven assists. Joel Embiid added 14 points and 11 rebounds in his return from an illness and Dominick Barlow had 12 points, eight rebounds, two steals, and two blocks. Here are the three biggest takeaways after the win: Getting back to the basics defensively Let's be real. There has been a lot of slippage for this team on the defensive end of the floor in recent games. The Pacers are a team that feature some real offensive threats and it was time for the Sixers to get back after it on that end of the floor. They were stifling in this one and forced the Pacers to take some horrible shots and they were out of rhythm all night long as the Sixers were able to handle business on that end of the floor. "We understand that our calling card ultimately is going to be the defensive end and we got to defend at a high level," said James. sports.title: Defining week for Republic of Ireland in World Cup bid
sports.description: Republic of Ireland are aiming to reach a second successive World Cup [Getty Images] The Republic of Ireland are potentially just 180 minutes away from booking their spot at consecutive Women's World Cups. Standing in their way to next year's tournament are familiar foes in the form of Poland, who they beat twice in their qualifying group. They will play the Poles twice more, with the first leg in Gdansk on Tuesday, 1 December and the second leg at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin on Saturday, 5 December with the winner securing their place on the plane to Brazil. Ahead of a potentially defining week for Carla Ward and her players, BBC Sport NI looks at how they are gearing up for the massive play-off games. Republic of Ireland boss Ward signs new contract Mustaki out of World Cup play-off with knee injury Ward's new deal overshadowed by Mustaki's injury Mustaki ruptured her ACL while playing for Nottingham Forest against Liverpool [Getty Images] It's been a mix of good and bad news for Republic of Ireland in the build-up to the two games. There was the welcome announcement on Monday that head coach Ward had signed a new contract until the end of the Euro 2029 campaign. Ward's current deal was set to expire at the end of this World Cup qualification campaign and it will be a relief to the manager and players that she that will stay, irrespective of how the play-off pans out. It offers stability that the Irish have lacked in recent years and it is certainly well deserved given she has overseen 12 victories in her 19 games, including promotion to League A and excellent performances in their group against the Poles, France and Netherlands. Ward's legacy will really be enhanced if she can follow Vera Pauw in leading the team to another World Cup and she can fully focus on doing so now that her future has been resolved before this window. That announcement had followed the devastating blow that Ward had been dealt earlier on Monday, the confirmation that defender Chloe Mustaki would miss the play-off with a knee injury. Mustaki, who has been integral for the Irish as a left-sided centre-back under Ward, ruptured her anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) in action for Nottingham Forest against Liverpool in the League Cup last week. Ward said it was "a really difficult setback" for Mustaki, who also suffered an ACL injury in 2020 and was diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma aged 19. Her club announced that she would miss the rest of the season and she would also likely have to sit out the World Cup if the Irish do qualify. Ward did not call up a replacement to her 24-strong squad that gathered in Dublin on Tuesday and with everyone else fully fit, she will hope they have enough to get over the line even without Mustaki. The Wildcats had one final opportunity to steal a win at Rupp Arena, but a costly mistake on the baseline with only five seconds left left them with virtually no chance of doing that. And as Pope made clear after the game, the blame rests entirely on his shoulders. “That’s 100% on me, guys. That is 100% me. Somehow that changed to a live ball in my mind, and I messed that up. Trailing 73–71 in overtime at Rupp Arena, Kentucky forced a turnover when a Wichita State pass went out of bounds under the basket with roughly five seconds left. Following a timeout, Pope drew up a play where inbounder Alex Wilkins passed the ball along the baseline to teammate Mason Williams, who was standing out of bounds. However, under NCAA rules, a player can only run the baseline and pass to a teammate standing out of bounds following a made basket, not after a dead-ball turnover. technology.title: Quantum: 'Five years, that's all we got…'
technology.description: SC26 in Chicago had the usual quantum booths, discussions, and hallway optimism. A lot of people were talking about integration with classical HPC and Slurm scheduling for quantum processors, co-design platforms, and GPU-accelerated error correction tools. That part is real and useful. What was harder to find was any result that changed the basic math on when quantum systems will actually do something a supercomputer can't already handle better. I had a long conversation in St. Louis (SC25) with a contact who works deep in quantum and has spent decades in HPC. He's not a skeptic for sport, although that can be fun, sure. Over a grifted free dinner in Chicago (the best kind), his take this year remains the same: the hype keeps outrunning the error rates. Quantum computers generate too many errors to give usable answers on anything interesting. Fixing that is the whole game. And that's a five-year game, minimum. Much like the Bowie anthem in the title. Qubits by the numbers There are two kinds of qubits. Physical qubits are the actual hardware: ions, superconducting circuits, and atoms in a trap. Logical qubits are the ones that do the computation. Each logical qubit is built out of many physical ones so the system can detect and correct errors while it runs. With the traditional surface-code approach, one logical qubit often needs somewhere between 500 and 2,000 physical qubits backing it up, depending on the hardware and the code. One logical qubit by itself is useless. Estimates for basic scientific modeling and small-scale simulation sit in the 100-to-500 logical-qubit range. Take the midpoint of 300. At the low end of the overhead that is 150,000 physical qubits. At the high end it is several million. That is only for early science. Commercial work like molecular mapping for pharma, large optimization problems, complex financial models, pushes into the thousands of logical qubits. National-security and encryption-related work sits even higher. Those numbers have not magically shrunk. A system that can map a modestly sized drug molecule, or run a materials simulation that is still too slow on classical machines, is the kind of workload people actually mean when they talk about useful quantum advantage. Until the logical-qubit counts get there with error rates low enough to finish the job, those problems stay on the machines we already know how to build. Ok, so let's just scale it up This is the world of HPC, we know how to scale stuff, right? Yes, but this isn't a matter of adding a few more racks. Scaling to an additional few hundred thousand physical qubits is not a rack or two or ten. It's probably a dedicated building with its own cryogenics, control electronics, and power draw that is still measured in megawatts even before you get useful logical capacity. technology.description: What's the difference between just-for-fun demo hacks, and serious carefully designed large-scale software architecture? It's the quick-and-dirty jobs that end up transforming computing. A blog post earlier this week called 2035 came early led the Reg FOSS desk down what we thought was a fascinating, and possibly quite scary, rabbit-hole… but it turned out to be an entire warren. We thought we were still in 2026, but in turns out that in some ways, tech just leaped forward a decade. To try to convey the point of this blog post – why what had been just a fun clever little hack has the potential to take half a century of OS and hypervisor design and throw it out of the nearest window – will take quite a lot of unpacking. If you bear with us, we will try to walk you through it. To get started, we need to go back a decade or more. Stick with this: there are laughs, as well as hammers taken to beloved ideas. The year of 2035 and the ideas around that come from a remarkable talk by Gary Bernhardt of Destroy All Software, which is both funny and highly educational. It will really massively assist understanding what this article and the technology is all about if you have the time to watch the talks. The Reg FOSS desk is not at all fond of spoken-word video as a medium – we much prefer to read than listen – but the three talks we're going to mention are golden, among the very best presentations this century in all of computing and IT. Seriously, they are worth your time. As a preface, before we go into Bernhardt's half-hour information-dense talk, let's warm up with a four-minute funny one. But first, let's look at the context for that. Step 0: JavaScript is the language of web programming In 2009, Jeff Atwood laid this out in an article called All Programming is Web Programming . It's still coming true today. Software is getting very blurred around the edges. The entire SaaS industry means that massive organizations run on web apps. Tech like Electron embeds a web browser inside JavaScript apps built in Node.js, while Progressive Web Apps make websites look like local program windows. The most popular desktop Linux in the world is ChromeOS Flex, which doesn't support local native applications at all. Everything is browser windows, even the desktop. It's all built in JavaScript. And yet… Step 1: JavaScript is kind of weird and kind of bad. Bernhardt made this case in 2012, with a celebrated lightning talk called Wat , from the CodeMash conference in 2012. Wat walks through a whole list of examples of how JavaScript is a very strange programming language and does very strange things that are not at all what you might expect. Some of the jokes will make more sense to programmers, but we reckon anyone who has ever fought with a recalcitrant bit of software will get some laughs from it – and that probably applies to all readers of The Register. Step 2: JavaScript is in the process of conquering the world. Bernhardt moved on to much bigger ideas at PyCon 2014

technology.title: Smartphone shipments face another bleak year before modest 2028 comeback
technology.description: Global smartphone shipments are forecast to fall 14 percent this year and another 6 percent in 2027, with a recovery not expected until 2028. That's the outlook from Counterpoint Research's latest Smartphone Market Outlook Tracker , which points to rising memory costs and constrained supplies as continuing pressure on handset makers and buyers. The downturn was particularly sharp in the third quarter: IDC and Omdia estimated year-on-year shipment declines of 22 percent and 20 percent respectively, as rising prices and component shortages squeezed the market. Don't expect things to get better in the short term, as Counterpoint forecasts another 6 percent drop during 2027. But it believes that the market may see a 6 percent rebound in 2028, as memory supplies improve, pricing begins to stabilize, and pent-up demand for replacement phones returns. The 2026 outlook has been shaped by sharply rising component costs, particularly for DRAM and NAND flash. According to IDC , memory costs have risen approximately 350 percent since last year and are still climbing. As Reg readers will be well aware by now, this has been blamed on the memory manufacturers prioritizing output of high-margin chips to go into AI servers and GPU accelerators, creating a shortage of the mainstream components that are needed for devices like PCs and phones. Vendors have responded by raising prices, reducing memory configurations, and withdrawing lower-cost models. As The Register previously reported , memory costs accounted for almost 60 percent of the total bill of materials in sub-$400 smartphones during Q1 of 2026. For 2027, Counterpoint warns the outlook is for continued tight mobile DRAM supply, further price increases for low-power DDR (LPDDR) memory, and limited evidence to suggest short-term capacity increases. "The 2026 decline was initially expected to mark the low point of the cycle, but the memory situation has remained more restrictive than anticipated," said principal analyst Yang Wang. "Mobile memory allocation is still being displaced by AI and server demand, while higher costs are taking longer to move through handset portfolios and retail channels. The result is a much weaker 2027, particularly for lower priced devices and price sensitive markets." Global shipments are forecast to rebound by 6 percent in 2028, but that would bring shipments only roughly back to this year's already shrunken level, rather than hitting the peak of previous years. Counterpoint cautions that the scale of the rebound will depend on how quickly lower component costs translate into retail pricing. A speedy improvement in mobile memory allocation during the second half of 2027 could bring replacement demand forward and swell shipments, but continued competition from the AI market or another round of handset price increases would hinder recovery. Papers presented to its Audit Committee this week put the combined cost of the original implementation, which went live in 2022, and this year's reimplementation at £128.1 million, against £19.96 million forecast in the 2019 business case [PDF]. The report , from program director Philip Macpherson, said the project's funding allocation had previously reached £157 million. The report said the new Oracle Fusion system went live in August without any priority-one or "showstopper" issues. "The program has now moved into the Post Go Live Support phase where [it] continues to provide extra support but slowly transitions towards 'Business As Usual' operating procedures," the report said. It is an understatement to say the same was not true of the first attempt to move the council's finance, HR, and payroll systems off its legacy R/3 SAP system to more modern software. The first project started in 2019 and was supposed to go live in April 2021, but was delayed by a year. After the council started to use the system in April 2022, it soon became beset by a series of serious problems. Although the council had planned to implement Oracle "out-of-the-box," it created several customizations, including a bank reconciliation system that failed to function properly. The council struggled to understand its cash position and was unable to produce auditable accounts . It has spent more than £5 million on manual workaround labor . The system move also contributed to it becoming effectively bankrupt , an event it failed to foresee due to the malfunctioning finance system. It later emerged that officials ignored a "red" warning prior to the go-live date. They were explicitly told the system could cause late payments, a failure to collect debt, and incorrect accounting if it went live. Officials gave the go-ahead regardless. The council decided to reimplement Oracle from scratch, while running the current system as best it could and implementing off-the-shelf software CivicaPay , now rebranded as Civica Income Management. Despite the apparently trouble-free relaunch, the true cost to the council is likely higher than the projected £128.1 million implementation bill. For a start, the original £19 million budget was supposed to support the software implementation for schools , but that was excluded from the reimplementation. Secondly, the council expected significant savings from moving to Oracle in 2022 through greater efficiency. The 2019 business case booked £27 million in savings from 2019 to 2031, for example. A 2024 analysis by Audit Reform Lab, based at the University of Sheffield, estimated that the disaster's direct and indirect financial impact, including lost savings and deteriorating tax collection, would reach £216.5 million by April 2026. technology.title: UK government rejects national consultation on AI datacenters
technology.description: The UK government has rejected calls for a UK-wide public consultation on the environmental impacts of AI datacenters, despite a petition attracting more than 39,000 signatures. Campaign group Protect the Wild launched the petition last month, calling for a national consultation that would consider whether further expansion should be restricted, paused, or halted until those impacts are properly understood and addressed. The nonprofit says the petition smashed the 10,000 signature threshold above which a government response is required in just three days, and the total stood at over 39,000 as this article was being prepared. In its response, published on November 23, the government ruled out the requested UK-wide environmental consultation, saying individual projects' impacts should be addressed through the planning process. It pointed instead to a separate consultation on its draft datacenter planning policy, open until January 8, 2027. "Datacenters are vital to the UK's digital economy. They underpin the digital services that people rely on every day, including public services, healthcare and the way people work. They also provide the infrastructure needed to develop and use AI," the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST) says. "Building more capacity in the UK will support economic growth and innovation, while strengthening national resilience and ensuring the UK is well placed to realize the opportunities presented by AI." But it adds that the government recognizes the environmental impacts of bit barns are real and must be understood and mitigated, and this is one of the reasons why it established the Data Centre Covenant tests. This Covenant, published last month, sets out tests all compute sheds "are encouraged to meet," while "strategic datacenters" are required to meet them to qualify for additional government assistance. The government has yet to define which datacenters qualify as "strategic," saying it will publish further details and eligibility criteria in due course. Qualifying projects could receive help securing power and accelerating planning. Briefly, the Covenant tests are that operators cover any energy costs they create, so that communities do not have to pick up the bill; that they invest in local communities; adhere to the highest environmental standards; create jobs and drive reindustrialization; and provide secure and reliable access to their compute resources. If this has a ring of familiarity, it is because President Trump earlier this year introduced a Ratepayer Protection Pledge , under which hyperscalers and AI companies agreed to protect US consumers from any bill shocks due to the energy and infrastructure requirements of their datacenter projects. It seems that where the US leads, the UK still often follows. science.title: Dropping missiles from orbit? 2 European companies sign agreement to study the idea
science.description:
Julian Dossett is a freelance writer living in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. In 2022 and 2024, his travel writing earned IRMA Awards. Previously, he worked as a staff writer at CNET. He graduated from Texas State University in San Marcos in 2011 with a B.A. in philosophy. He owns a large collection of sci-fi pulp magazines from the 1960s.

A pair of companies in Europe have signed an agreement to study the feasibility of developing weapons that can be dropped from orbit. Atmos, a space company known for its Phoenix reusable reentry vehicle , will work with MBDA, Europe's largest missile manufacturer, on the new project. "We are assessing how proven defense systems and new orbital technologies can be combined to strengthen Europe's conventional deterrence and enable future defense capabilities," Sebastian Klaus, the CEO of Atmos Space Cargo, said in a statement on Nov. 18. The system that the companies are investigating is called Precision Orbital Deep Strike, or PODS. The companies said that their initial scope will center on design and feasibility, as well as technology integration. Atmos and MBDA also said this work could lead to demonstrations, but the companies' announcement makes it clear that any deployment or use would be subject to the approval of governmental and military authorities. "The initiative also directly supports MBDA's broader strategic vision in the space domain, reinforcing both space for defense and the defense of space," Thomas Gottschild, MBDA Deutschland managing director, said in the same statement. This news comes a few months after Chief of Space Operations Gen. Douglas Schiess said that the U.S. Space Force operates orbital weapons . "Let me be crystal clear: Today, Guardians operate on-orbit weapons that can defend the joint force against space-enabled attacks," Schiess said during a conferenace presentation on Sept. 15 ("Guardians" refers to Space Force personnel.) Last year, Atmos' Phoenix capsule got its first test run in space. The cargo-return technology launched aboard a Space X Falcon 9 rocket during a rideshare mission in February 2025. Atmos tested out the inflatable heat shields it has been working on to help future space-manufactured cargo make it through Earth's atmosphere in one piece. "Orbital transportation and return form a new layer of strategic infrastructure, and infrastructure determines what Europe can achieve on its own terms," Klaus said in the Nov 18 statement.
